thirtySeconds: KeithK75 won the net race at Shinnecock by eight shots, posting +1 while HamSammich settled for +9 and MashedBROtato trailed at +15. The challengers were not exactly threatening the clubhouse furniture: Dan94 and DREADFUL both finished +27, with IUDoc92 at +32 and Leroy4522 at +28. Keith also took gross at -3, backed by a ridiculous 17.79 total strokes gained, including 8.05 on approach and 6.68 around the greens. Dan was the raw runner-up at +19, but the rest of the field turned Shinnecock into a long-form argument against ball-striking.
latestTournamentTeaser: KeithK75 ran away with the net title at Shinnecock Hills, winning by eight shots at +1 and taking gross too at -3. Behind him, Dan94’s +19 gross was the only remotely tidy raw round in a field that otherwise treated fairways and greens like optional side quests.

carnage.name: Dan94
carnage.commentary: This started with a 229-yard drive into deep rough, then became a nine-shot hostage situation. Dan needed five more swings just to find the fairway, stalled at zero yards to the hole, finally reached the green from 27 yards, and two putts plus a gimmie later had converted a par five into a four-over crime scene.

carnage.name: IUDoc92
carnage.commentary: A 163-yard tee ball into deep rough was merely the opening act. From there came sand, repeated fairway misses, a 30-yard pitch to 26 feet, and a 25-foot putt left one foot short. Eight shots: the hole never got better, it just eventually ran out of places to go.

carnage.name: DREADFUL
carnage.commentary: The first ball found deep rough from 119 yards, and the recovery plan immediately dissolved. Four swings later the ball was still wandering between fairway and deep rough, followed by a 19-yard pitch and an 11-footer that finished one foot away. Seven on a par three, with the tap-in doing all the administrative work.

carnage.name: Leroy4522
carnage.commentary: A 213-yard miss into deep rough turned into a 12-yard approach and then a putting marathon: 41 feet, 20 feet, 14 feet, and finally a three-footer. Eight shots total, seven net, and enough lag putting to make the hole feel like a hostage negotiation.

carnage.name: HamSammich
carnage.commentary: Ham’s 144-yard tee shot went deep rough, and every attempted escape found more deep rough until shot four finally reached the fairway. From eight yards out he still needed a six-yard pitch and a six-footer before the gimmie arrived. Seven gross, six net—somehow the handicap department found a coupon in the wreckage.

carnage.name: KeithK75
carnage.commentary: Even the champ had one ugly patch: fairway, green, then deep rough on the third swing, with the shot sequence skipping from three to five because the data skips shot four. He eventually reached the green from 23 yards and made the 11-footer for a seven, which is what dominance looks like when it briefly trips over its own shoelaces.

carnage.name: MashedBROtato
carnage.commentary: A 130-yard tee ball into rough was followed by a 38-yard detour to the fairway and a 21-yard pitch to 19 feet. The 17-footer finished two feet short, leaving a tap-in for five. Two over on a par three: not catastrophic by this field’s standards, but still a full tour of the neighborhood.

players.name: KeithK75
players.tagline: Approach play so sharp it needed a warning label
players.body: KeithK75 won both competitions, taking net at +1 and gross at -3, with an eight-shot net cushion over HamSammich. The numbers were brutal: 17.79 total strokes gained, led by 8.05 on approach and 6.68 in the short game, plus 2.44 putting. He hit 10 greens, made four birdies, avoided every bogey and double bogey, and needed only 24 putts with no three-putts. His worst hole was still a seven after a deep-rough detour, a skipped shot entry between three and five, and a made 11-footer. Across seven prior starts, Keith already owned a 1.57 average gross finish, four gross wins, and 12.4 average total SG; this round confirms that the raw-golf machine is not making much noise because it is too busy winning.

players.name: HamSammich
players.tagline: The longest drive was not the longest part of the hole
players.body: HamSammich grabbed second in net at +9, but the raw card was +37, third gross, and the gap between those numbers tells the story. He gained 2.37 putting and 0.66 off the tee, but lost 2.06 on approach and 1.58 tee to green, while hitting only four greens. Seven bogeys and four doubles left plenty of damage for the handicap math to clean up. The worst hole featured a deep-rough festival from the tee through shot three before he finally reached the fairway, then needed a six-yard pitch and a six-footer for a net six. His five-start history is built on strong net finishes but negative SG overall at -2.19 per appearance, so this was another net result carried by survival rather than clean ball-striking.

players.name: MashedBROtato
players.tagline: Thirty-five miles per hour of drive and three fairways of accuracy
players.body: MashedBROtato finished third net at +15 and fourth gross at +39, gaining 4.79 strokes total with a useful 3.07 on approach and 4.77 tee to green. The problem was the scorecard: only three fairways and six greens, followed by eight bogeys and two doubles. He did find three birdies, including a 25-footer on a net eagle at the notable 12th, but the broader round was too leaky to hold together. The worst hole was a five on a par three after rough, fairway, a 21-yard pitch, and a 17-footer that stopped two feet short. His seven-start profile is volatile, with a slightly negative average total SG of -0.06 despite one net and one gross win; this was a better ball-striking day than the score suggests, just not a clean one.

players.name: Dan94
players.tagline: A fairway-finding machine with one deeply cursed par five
players.body: Dan94 was the raw runner-up at +19 and finished fourth net at +27, a sharp reminder that net is the league scoreboard. He gained 6.79 total strokes, with 3.63 on approach and 5.71 tee to green, hit eight fairways, and had zero doubles or three-putts. But eight bogeys erased the tidy parts, and the par five disaster was spectacular: a 229-yard drive into deep rough, five more swings before reaching the green area, then a 19-footer and gimmie for nine. His seven-start history remains much kinder to his gross golf—1.71 average gross finish and 11.97 average total SG—than to his net results, with no net wins. This round fit that profile exactly: quality raw work, expensive mistakes, and no net trophy.

players.name: DREADFUL
players.tagline: The ball-striking filed a restraining order against the hole
players.body: DREADFUL finished +27 net and +75 gross, with a total SG of -12.21 that was negative everywhere: -6.09 off the tee, -1.34 approach, -0.44 short game, and -4.34 putting. Three greens, 35 putts, three three-putts, four bogeys, and eight doubles made the scorecard look like it had been assembled during a power outage. The worst hole was a seven on a par three after the tee shot found deep rough, the next escape found fairway, the next stayed short, and shot four went back to deep rough before a 12-footer and tap-in. His seven prior starts already showed -6.33 average total SG, 5.71 greens per round, and 4.14 doubles per appearance; Shinnecock did not challenge that profile so much as underline it in permanent marker.

players.name: IUDoc92
players.tagline: One holed-out highlight surrounded by a lot of rough draft
players.body: IUDoc92 finished sixth net at +32 and fifth gross at +72, losing 10.21 total strokes. The tee-to-green number was -7.84, short game -3.90, putting -2.36, and only two greens were hit. The scorecard did contain a genuine bright spot: a hole-out from 18 yards for a net eagle, plus a made nine-footer elsewhere. Unfortunately, the worst hole went the other direction, with deep rough off the tee, sand, repeated fairway misses, and a 30-yard pitch before an eight-foot-something finish from 26 feet. His seven-start history shows a strong net average finish of 5.43 but -9.32 total SG per appearance, so the net-friendly result remains possible while the underlying golf keeps demanding emergency repairs.

players.name: Leroy4522
players.body: Leroy4522 finished seventh in both net and gross, at +28 and +55, while losing 11.21 total strokes. He hit one green, lost 3.55 off the tee, 2.04 on approach, 4.05 around the green, and another 1.56 with the putter. The one-green performance came with 36 putts and four three-putts, although the 107 feet of putts made shows he at least got plenty of reps. His worst hole required deep rough, fairway, more fairway, rough, and then three putts from 32 feet for an eight. Seven prior starts point to a familiar problem: -5.74 average total SG and -4.36 on approach, with a 6.86 average net finish. Shinnecock was not a break from the pattern; it was the pattern wearing a louder shirt.

stateOfLeague: KeithK75’s two-competition sweep strengthens an already clear profile: seven prior starts, four gross wins, two net wins, and now another dominant raw performance at 17.79 total SG. Dan94 remains the strongest gross challenger on the evidence, but HamSammich’s net runner-up finish shows how far the net race can separate from raw scoring; the leaderboard is not simply ranking the prettiest golf.
